items.summary: plvs GPU port (ORB/FAST feature kernels + libelas-gpu + libsgm stereo) compiles for gfx90a against the MOAT OpenCV-with-HIP fork but is blocked on: (1) OpenCV core PR #29285 + opencv_contrib PR #4147 landing upstream so cv::cuda-on-ROCm is a consumable released dep; (2) building the full non-GPU SLAM stack (PCL/Pangolin/DBoW2/g2o/voxblox/chisel) + stereo datasets to validate on GPU, including verifying libsgm wave64 disparity correctness (WARP_SIZE=64 reductions, may need logical-32 rework per the OpenCV cudastereo conclusion). Resume when OpenCV PRs land. Fork moat-port HEAD f932ab5.

plvs gfx1201 HIP device code is PROVEN on Windows (libsgm stereo PASS: coverage 0.841, agreement 0.972, matches Linux), but the full mono-TUM SLAM cannot run on Windows: bundled ROS-adjacent CPU libs (DBoW2, g2o, line_descriptor, voxblox, open_chisel, chisel_server, voxblox_server) hardcode Unix .so/.a outputs in their CMakeLists; PCL unavailable (not in vcpkg, github TLS-blocked); Pangolin version mismatch (vcpkg 0.9.5 vs required fe57db5/v0.6+patch); main CMakeLists uses -fPIC/-pthread/pkg_check_modules(GLFW) without WIN32 guards. Upstream Windows-portability gap, not an AMD/HIP defect. gfx1201 is redundant/optional Windows tier and NOT PR-required (Linux completed). To complete: Windows-guard the bundled-lib CMakeLists + supply PCL/Pangolin, or validate the SLAM path on gfx1101 instead.

Rescan with the fixed scan_nvidia: include/cuda/ vendors pre-2017 CUDA samples EULA-pointer headers (helper_cuda.h, helper_string.h). No licence ruling on the vendored copies is recorded; needs a person's confirmation.
